subject: Version stamp and dependency clarifications for Sailfin-v2 onboarding
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: prodops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sailfin-v2 integration — tokenizer/latency questions and versioning request

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our infra team dug in overnight and surfaced two quick blockers before we can sign-off on the PoC:

1) Tokenizer parity — we saw a mismatch in token counts between your hosted endpoint and our local tokenizer for a few payloads (examples attached). Can you confirm which tokenizer byte-order and BPE vocabulary you're using for Sailfin-v2?

2) Version pinning/upgrade guarantee — we need an explicit version stamp and a guarantee that any minor runtime changes won't change tokenization or the default quantization profile for the pinned model during our trial window. Otherwise we'll see floating latency/cost numbers in our benchmarks.

Can you point us to any compatibility matrix or short-run checklist so our platform team can sign the integration readiness? We want to avoid re-running evals mid-PoC.

Best,
Jane
Platform Ops — Acme Corp

Attachment: examples_token_mismatch.txt (text)
Attachment: ACME_Sailfin_integration_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sailfin-v2 integration — tokenizer/latency questions and versioning request

Hi Jane — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. Short answers up-front, then action items below.

1) Tokenizer parity: Sailfin-v2 uses our standard UTF-8 BPE encoder with little-endian byte ordering; vocab is sailfin_v2_vocab_v1.json. The mismatch you observed typically comes from two causes: (a) hidden control characters in the test inputs, or (b) newline normalization differences. Laura, can you share the exact tokenizer command we recommend for on-prem tests?

2) Version pinning: we can provide a version stamp for the model artifact (sailfin-v2@20260815) and a runtime compatibility guarantee scoped to the PoC (30 days). That guarantee covers tokenizer, byte-order, and default quantization profile (q4_0). It excludes infra-level kernel swaps that we surface in advance.

Action items I propose:
- Redwood: produce a one-page compatibility matrix + a short script to reproduce the tokenizer used in Hosted (laura) — ETA: EOD Monday.
- Acme: share the minimal failing examples (sounds like you've attached some; we'll run them) — ETA: Monday morning.
- Both: create an INF Jira to track any changes during the PoC (I'll open INF-9081).

I'll attach the provisional compatibility matrix and the checklist for sign-off. If that scope works, we'll stamp sailfin-v2 for your PoC and add a short rollback runbook.

Markus
Director, Product Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Attachment: sailfin-v2-compat-matrix.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: provisional_rollforward_runbook.md (text)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-30T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sailfin-v2 integration — tokenizer/latency questions and versioning request

Jane — jumping in with the tokenizer repro and a few clarifications.

- Repro command (same as we run on Hosted):
  python -m redwood.tokenize --model sailfin-v2 --input sample.txt --output tokens.json --byte_order little --normalize-newlines True

- Vocab: sailfin_v2_vocab_v1.json (we ship this as part of the artifact tarball). If you run the repro with the exact file attached it should match token counts. If it doesn't, please send the failing sample and the output of the repro command.

- Latency/quant: default hosted profile is q4_0 with our kernel selection that favors throughput for sequence lengths > 512. If your benchmark uses mostly short prompts (<128 tokens) we can switch to a low-latency kernel (config: kernel_mode=low_latency) for the PoC. That will change throughput and per-token cost; we'll note it in the compatibility matrix.

Karthik — can you confirm whether the runtime guarantee needs to include a clause about kernel swaps for specific GPU families? Acme's infra note suggested they run across T4 and A100.

Laura Bennett
Staff Engineer, Runtime Compatibility — Redwood Inference

> On 2026-08-29T11:04:00-07:00, markus.klein@redwood.com wrote:
> > Short answers up-front, then action items below...
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sailfin-v2 integration — tokenizer/latency questions and versioning request

Thanks all — quick policy clarifications and next steps from infra/compat side:

- Kernel swap clause: we will not perform silent kernel swaps that affect tokenizer semantics or the default quantization profile during the agreed PoC window (sailfin-v2@20260815, 30 days). We may, however, ship non-semantic micro-optimizations (perf kernels) for specific hardware; those are allowed provided we validate no tokenizer/decoded-output regressions in our CI and notify Acme.

- GPU families: we can specify the supported families for the stamped build: T4, A100. If Acme expects other hardware, let's get a short compatibility matrix in INF-9081.

Next steps (owners):
- Laura: publish the repro script + compat matrix to the Drive folder and link in INF-9081 — due 2026-08-31 EOD.
- Markus: add the PoC version stamp to the Master Intake doc and share the signed checklist back to Acme.
- Jane/Acme: confirm whether you want the low-latency kernel route for short prompts or the default throughput profile — reply here with preference.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
